runs.text: The sky appears blue during the day because the Earth's atmosphere scatters sunlight in all directions. Shorter blue wavelengths scatter more than other colors, so the sky looks blue to our eyes. At sunset, the sun is lower on the horizon, and its light has to travel through more atmosphere. This longer path scatters the shorter blue and green wavelengths out of the line of sight, allowing the longer red and orange wavelengths to dominate and create the red sunset.

cascade.transcript: Why is the sky blue during the day?And why does it turn red at sunset?
cascade.reply: The sky is blue because Earth's atmosphere scatters shorter blue light waves more easily than other colors. At sunset, light must travel through more atmosphere, scattering away the blue and leaving only the longer red wavelengths to reach your eyes.
